entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""Then take the time to consider it,..."

entries.speaker: Player_Romus

entries.dialogueText: "I don't need to *consider* what's already obvious. The houses will grumble, they always do. But they will comply."

entries.dialogueText: "Doubling their forces will double their influence as well."

entries.title: Player_Romus: ""More soldiers mean stronger houses..."
entries.dialogueText: "More soldiers mean stronger houses, but it also means they are more dependent on the Crown. If they want to keep their new forces, they'll need to stay in line."

entries.title: Player_Romus: ""It will make them more loyal in th..."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Hugo narrowed his eyes, seemingly u..."
entries.dialogueText: Hugo narrowed his eyes, seemingly unimpressed by my sarcasm. A forceful smile appeared on his face.

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""Ah, of course! Who needs a Grand V..."
entries.dialogueText: "Ah, of course! Who needs a Grand Vizier when one has intestines?"

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""There's a fine line between grumbl..."
entries.dialogueText: "There's a fine line between grumbling and resisting, Romus."

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""Will they, now?""
entries.dialogueText: "Will they, now?"

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""Handing each of these houses twice..."
entries.dialogueText: "Handing each of these houses twice the number of soldiers under their personal command only empowers them to do the opposite of 'falling in line.'"

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""Handing each of these houses twice..."
entries.dialogueText: "Handing each of these houses twice the number of soldiers under their personal command is the very thing that could make 'grumbling' turn into something far worse."

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""And what do you propose, Uncle? Th..."
entries.dialogueText: "And what do you propose, Uncle? That we keep our forces weak? That the House armies stay tiny and underequipped while threats gather on our borders?"

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""You believe this decree could weak..."
entries.dialogueText: "You believe this decree could weaken the monarchy in the long run?"

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""You might be right. If they try to..."
entries.dialogueText: "You might be right. If they try to use their troops as their personal armies rather than the kingdom's forces, then we'll have a problem."

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""Naturally. Strategic foresight is..."
entries.dialogueText: "Naturally. Strategic foresight is overrated."

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""I do pride myself on efficiency.""
entries.dialogueText: "I do pride myself on efficiency."

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""I assume you came here for somethi..."
entries.dialogueText: "I assume you came here for something other than dramatic irony, Uncle."

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""I'm not here to question your auth..."
entries.dialogueText: "I'm not here to question your authority. But I must remind you that this decree doesn't only increase our forces. It shifts power in ways we can't control once the ink is dry."

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""I'm only here to challenge you bef..."
entries.dialogueText: "I'm only here to challenge you before your enemies do."

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""That depends on the Azaros and the..."
entries.dialogueText: "That depends on the Azaros and the Sazons. And on you."

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""Then the decree is completely just..."
entries.dialogueText: "Then the decree is completely justified."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Hugo blinked once, then exhaled slo..."
entries.dialogueText: Hugo blinked once, then exhaled slowly, pressing his lips together as if physically holding back a response.

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""You're the king, Romus. No one is..."
entries.dialogueText: "You're the king, Romus. No one is saying you haven’t thought this through."

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""I trust your judgement.""
entries.dialogueText: "I trust your judgement."

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""I will speak of this no more.""
entries.dialogueText: "I will speak of this no more."

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""Say what you will. But the absence..."
entries.dialogueText: "Say what you will. But the absence of fear has toppled more kings than I can count."

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""I'm here to challenge you before y..."
entries.dialogueText: "I'm here to challenge you before your enemies do."

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""That is precisely why I am here. S..."
entries.dialogueText: "That is precisely why I am here. So you do not ignore the potential fallout."

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""Because once you give a man an arm..."
entries.dialogueText: "Because once you give a man an army, the only thing stopping him from using it is whether he fears you enough."

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""Then I'll make sure they do.""
entries.dialogueText: "Then I'll make sure they do."

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""Then I remove them before they get..."
entries.dialogueText: "Then I remove them before they get that chance."

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""I appreciate the words, but fear w..."
entries.dialogueText: "I appreciate the words, but fear won't hold a nation together."

entries.speaker: Player_Romus
entries.title: Player_Romus: ""That's too dramatic.""
entries.dialogueText: "That's too dramatic."

entries.speaker: Hugo Toras
entries.title: Hugo Toras: ""No, but the absence of fear has to..."
